title: Increasing Productive Communications Statements in Esports Players
abstract: ABSTRACT Esports is a rapidly expanding competitive domain in which effective team communication is frequently identified as a critical determinant of performance, especially within the video game, League of Legends. Although applied behavior analysis (ABA) has extensively targeted communication in clinical populations, and organizational behavior management (OBM) has addressed communication in workplace settings, communication in esports has yet to be experimentally evaluated as behavior for change. The present study evaluated the effects of an OBM intervention package (task clarification, verbal and graphic feedback, and goal setting) on rates of productive in‐game communication among members of a collegiate League of Legends team. A concurrent multiple baseline design across four participants was used. The results showed increases in rates of productive communication, relative to baseline, across all four participants. These findings extend OBM applications to esports and demonstrate that team‐based communication in competitive gaming environments can be defined as specific behaviors, objectively measured, and improved using OBM techniques. Significance for behavioral interventions in esports and future research are discussed.
